profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: This bag is a lovely disaster: enough tee pop and approach flashes to keep the hope alive, then the short game and putting kick the door in and set the place on fire. The underlying shape is pretty clear over this window — he can find enough shots to look dangerous, but the cleanup crew is nonexistent. When it goes sideways, it goes sideways in a hurry, because the misses don’t just leak; they stack. Every so often there’s a decent ball-striking patch, and then the scoring clubs show up like rent collectors.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.profile: This dude can absolutely stripe an approach when the mood hits, which is why the rest of the file is so annoying. The tee ball and short game keep punching holes in his scorecard, and the putter is usually just there to witness the wreckage. He’s got enough iron play to survive ugly stretches, but not enough consistency off the tee or around the greens to make it easy on himself. The profile is mixed, volatile, and deeply unserious in the worst possible way: a guy who can hit a laser and still turn the whole hole into a hostage situation.

profiles.name: TEV_11
profiles.tagline: DRIVER BUILDS HOUSES, IRONS BURN THEM DOWN
profiles.profile: The tee game has flashes, but the approach play is the giant anchor dragging this whole operation into the swamp. There are enough ball-striking moments to make you think a breakout is around the corner, then the irons show up and start air-freighting the optimism into the woods. Short game has occasionally helped him steal a little dignity back, which is nice, because the raw scoring picture would otherwise be an entire crime scene. This file reads like a player who can absolutely create shots off the tee, then immediately asks the wedges and irons to apologize for him.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: This is a weirdly sneaky file because the short game keeps bailing out the rest of the junk. The tee and approach numbers are too flaky to call this cleanly stable, but the around-the-green work has been the one adult in the room. That said, when the irons go missing, the whole round starts looking like a guy trying to win a bar fight with a butter knife. There’s some scoring pop here, but it’s the kind that arrives dressed in duct tape and bad decisions.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.profile: This profile is all over the damn place, which is kind of the brand. There are real pop-up weeks where the whole bag clicks and he can beat a card into submission, but the baseline is still a lot of messy tee work and enough short-game chaos to make everyone age in dog years. The putter has been the friend in the group chat more often than not, which helps, because some of the ball-striking stretches are rough enough to make a caddie start looking for another job. Big ceiling, very questionable plumbing.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.profile: This file is what happens when the driver and irons decide to commit different crimes in the same round. The tee ball can absolutely get wild, and the approach play has too many crater holes to ignore, so the whole scoring setup ends up permanently on life support. There are occasional bursts where the putter or short game offers a lifeline, but the window here is mostly a parade of tee-to-green damage. He can make things look briefly playable, then the wedges and long game take turns lighting the match.
